title: Labels and the table
subtitle: Reading Central Otago and eating with it

steps.title: Reading the label
steps.body: Labels show the grape, Central Otago GI and often a sub-region, like Bannockburn or Gibbston. New Zealand's 85% rules apply, and screw caps are standard. Many producers are small and family-owned; some make single-vineyard wines.

steps.title: At the table
steps.body: Central Otago Pinot Noir suits lamb, especially New Zealand lamb, venison, duck, salmon and mushrooms. Its herbal, thyme notes suit herb-crusted meat. Pinot Gris and Riesling suit seafood and Asian food. Serve Pinot at 14 to 16 degrees; good examples age 8 to 12 years.

steps.prompt: Which dish suits Central Otago Pinot Noir?
steps.explanation: Its fruit and thyme notes suit herbed lamb.

steps.body: Queenstown, the nearby adventure-sports capital, makes Central Otago one of New Zealand's most visited wine regions.

steps.prompt: Central Otago Pinot Noir suits venison.
steps.explanation: Yes. Its fruit and acidity suit lean game.

steps.title: What you learned
points: Labels show the GI and often a sub-region
Pinot suits lamb, venison and salmon
